Zoe Park: noticed a bump in fn-tool-call fallbacks starting ~14:05 UTC. Console shows a lot of these labeled under the fallback route, which hides which customer routes are triggering the validation.
Rahul Singh: do we have a sample? what validator error?
Zoe Park: pasted from logs: \n``\ncall_payload: {"user_id": 42, "input": "hi", "meta": ["v1"] }\nvalidator: StructuredValidationError: data.meta must be object, got array at /meta\n``\nPriya Desai: That'll do it. The tool-hook expects meta as an object map. Current router policy routes to legacy-tool when validator throws non-fatal errors. Legacy-tool returns a degraded result which is billed to the original route_id, but console grouping uses the active route label so everything aggregates under legacy-tool.
Lin Zhao: minimal triage plan: 1) ramp sampling of validator rejects to 100% for 20m and store redacted payloads with trace id 2) add telemetry fields `validation.code` and `validation.path` to spans 3) create console quickfilter `validation.path:/meta` so product can inspect.
Nora Kim: billing complication: billing extractor uses `active_route` field at ingest time. If router re-routes earlier than billing tagging, charges end up mapped to fallback route. We need to decide ordering: tag billing before routing or tag both `original_route` and `final_route`.
Rahul Singh: For immediate mitigation we can change router to tag `original_route` into the request context before any reroute. That keeps chargeback stable while console can surface `final_route`.
Priya Desai: Agree. Also consider switching the fallback behavior from silent route->legacy to an explicit soft-reject mode that returns 422 with validation details plus an optional `suggested_fix` payload for common schema misses. That will push fixes upstream rather than relying on fallbacks.
Zoe Park: soft-reject sounds good but product will worry about noise. Maybe gate soft-reject behind canary and add a console setting per-organization to opt-in.
Lin Zhao: telemetry change is quick. I'll open a PR to: inject `original_route` into request.meta, emit `validation.reason` and `validation.path` tags, and sample payloads to secure S3 with trace id.
Nora Kim: I'll coordinate a billing extractor patch: add `original_route` and `final_route` as separate dimensions; keep existing `billable_route` mapping unchanged for chargeback until pm approves.
ops-bot: ALERT: fn-tool-call-fallback-rate > 0.6% (us-east-1, last 10m). Pager: eng-oncall.
Rahul Singh: For UX: Console team should add a small badge on route detail pages when `validation` tags show up, with a drilldown that groups by `validation.path` and lists sample traces. That avoids hiding root cause.
Priya Desai: Also let's add an aggregated metric: % of invocations that hit fallback due to validation vs due to capacity. Right now our fallback metric mixes causes. If we have separate counters for `fallback_cause=validation|capacity|timeout` we can alert more sensibly.
Nora Kim: Billing-bot: note that if we tag original_route earlier we must document for finance and run a backfill to correct last 24h reporting. I'll open PLAT-8801.
billing-bot: Created ticket PLAT-8801 for billing backfill and PLAT-8802 for extractor change.
Zoe Park: action list: Lin -> telemetry PR + sampling hook; Nora -> billing extractor PR + tickets; Rahul -> prototype soft-reject response (canary); Priya -> draft platform notice and coordinate canary; Nora + Finance -> schedule backfill. Will report status in 30m.
Priya Desai: small safety note: when adding original_route to request context, ensure we redact PII from samples and only store identifiers (e.g., tenant_id, route_id) not full payloads unless encrypted.
Lin Zhao: will add redaction and AWS KMS encryption on the S3 objects. Patch inbound.
Zoe Park: thanks all, keep this thread updated.
